name: Medial utility incision to the navicular and cuneiform
corridor: Extensile medial incision in the internervous plane between tibialis anterior and tibialis posterior, with essentially no major neurovascular structures, exposing the whole medial column

positioning.text: Position supine with the foot externally rotated so the medial border is accessible, under tourniquet control.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the medial border of the foot over the navicular, between the tibialis anterior and tibialis posterior tendons.

incision.text: Make the medial utility incision over the navicular, extendable proximally to the talonavicular joint or distally to the cuneiforms and first metatarsal base, full thickness with no undermining.

superficial_interval.text: Use the safe plane between tibialis posterior and tibialis anterior, cauterizing only small superficial veins since there are no major neurovascular structures in this region.

deep_interval.text: Expose the medial column subperiosteally, keeping soft-tissue stripping minimal to protect the navicular blood supply, and add a dorsomedial incision only if needed for articular reduction with at least a 5 cm skin bridge.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue with small veins, the tibialis anterior and posterior tendon interval, and the medial navicular, cuneiform, and first metatarsal.

structures_at_risk.text: There are no major neurovascular structures in this plane, but the navicular blood supply and the skin bridge to any second incision are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Over-stripping the navicular and a narrow skin bridge to a second incision are the danger zones.

retraction_hazards.text: Keep soft-tissue stripping minimal to protect navicular vascularity and maintain a full-thickness flap.

exposure.text: Exposes the whole medial first metatarsal, medial cuneiform, medial navicular, and head of the talus.

limitations.text: It exposes the medial column only; lateral or dorsal structures need an additional incision with an adequate skin bridge.

indications.text: Indicated for navicular, cuneiform, and first metatarsal base fractures and medial column reconstruction.

complications.text: Complications include navicular osteonecrosis from over-stripping and skin bridge necrosis when a second incision is used.

procedure_applications.condition: Extensile medial column exposure of the navicular, cuneiform, and first metatarsal base is needed

questions.question: Which internervous plane does the medial utility incision use?
questions.answer: Between the tibialis posterior and the tibialis anterior.

questions.question: What minimum skin bridge is kept when adding a dorsomedial incision?
Why keep soft-tissue stripping minimal at the navicular?
questions.answer: To avoid disrupting its blood supply and causing osteonecrosis.
